title: Tessera disk rescue: implementation gate
subtitle: Research is ready for a read-only build slice.
summary: The corpus now has 8,554 unique URLs across 58 inputs: 3,005 non-automated behavior records, 5,005 automated GitHub candidates, 30 Apple system facts, 426 owner or implementation facts, and 88 market signals. A separate agent may start the read-only rescue flow now. Raw owner actions and post-failure retry behavior remain gated on two open choices. No files were changed.

sections.title: Evidence snapshot
sections.intro: The source queue is large enough to guide the first build slice. Automated issue records stay separate until manual coding is complete.

rows: User and issue evidence used in pattern work
Issue pages 1 through 10; manual coding required

blocks.title: The agent can start now
blocks.text: Build the read-only Rescue path, scan coverage, ranked review, local case save, and tests. Keep risky and owner-managed items protected. Research continues during implementation.

sections.title: What the latest batch adds
sections.intro: Pages 5 through 10 added 3,217 candidates through the logged-in GitHub CLI. They sharpen state boundaries, but they do not grant permission to delete.

items: Game paths mix payloads with saves, mods, launcher registration, external volumes, partial transfers, and runtime state.
Package paths mix shared stores with local sources, locks, offline rebuild needs, and project materializations.
Profiles mix exact caches with sessions, credentials, drafts, local history, offline data, and workspace databases.
Communication paths mix attachments with exports, encryption, sync, local databases, and active writers.
All 5,005 records are discovery candidates. They must not change a safety rule until a person codes them.

sections.title: Development gate
sections.intro: The first implementation slice has a safe boundary and does not need to wait for the open product choices.

rows: Rescue entry, scan phases, coverage, named measurements, ranked candidates, exact-path review, local case save, and no-mutation tests
Raw backup or VM actions, generic profile or communication deletion, permanent deletion, silent retry, and background mutation
Safe, review, and protected rows with owner handoff and clear reasons
Any action that depends on a verified restore copy, guest state, or post-failure policy
Hard holds for active, unclear, owner-managed, sync, backup, virtual-disk, profile, and communication state
Broad rules based only on names such as node_modules, Cache, or System Data

blocks.title: Do not cross the gate
blocks.text: Round 7 decides backup and virtual-disk owner action, recovery proof, and host plus guest evidence. Round 10 decides pause behavior, blocker explanation, and background work after failure. Until then, use hard holds and owner handoffs.

sections.title: Implementation plan
sections.intro: Use the existing Tessera flow. Keep the first diff small and test the real macOS path.

items: Trace the existing scan, suggestion, view-model, and Trash flow in an isolated Tessera space.
Add Rescue entry and the needs_rescue, scanning, diagnosing, and plan_ready states.
Add the shared identity and owner-state gate. Report path, volume, type, coverage, permission, process, lock, sync, logical size, physical size, and measurement source.
Build ranked review rows. Preselect only high-confidence rebuildable items. Keep all unknown or owner-managed rows review-only or protected.
Add local resumable case state. Revalidate identity, coverage, owner, and capacity before any future staging or Trash move.
Add tests for no mutation during scan, stale paths, permission gaps, active writers, measurement mismatch, per-item results, and local-only case data.
Run the rendered macOS window at the supported sizes. Then return to the research loop for every new decision.

sections.title: Round 7: choose recovery behavior
sections.intro: Backups, snapshots, Docker images, and VM bundles have restore value and owner-controlled state.

blocks.title: Choose the recovery boundary
blocks.description: The recommended choices protect recovery objects while showing the exact owner action and measured state.

fields.label: 1. What should Tessera do with backups and VM bundles?
fields.description: A large bundle may be a current restore path, an old device backup, a live environment, or an owner-managed disk image.

options.label: Owner app only
options.description: Keep device backups, Time Machine, Docker, Parallels, UTM, and similar bundles protected; show the exact owner next step.

options.label: Review raw path
options.description: Show the exact path, state, and a strong warning; allow inspection without placing it in safe staging.

fields.label: 2. What proof should be required before reclaim?
fields.description: A Trash move cannot recreate a lost restore point, guest state, or persistent volume.

options.label: Require verified copy
options.description: Require a verified backup or restore point and show when it was last checked before a source-aware reclaim.

options.label: Warn and review
options.description: Show the missing proof and let the user continue to a review step after a stronger warning.

fields.label: 3. What evidence should a disk-image row show?
fields.description: Host file size, physical allocation, guest capacity, snapshots, and runtime state can disagree.

options.label: Host, guest, and runtime
options.description: Show logical and physical size, guest or runtime state, snapshots, owner, and restore role when known.

options.label: Host file only
options.description: Keep the row compact and show only the host file size until the user opens details.

fields.label: Your notes
fields.description: Name a backup, VM, snapshot, owner app, or restore boundary that must shape the first version.
fields.placeholder: For example: never delete a Time Machine or Docker bundle; show me the owner action and last verified restore point.

sections.title: Round 10: choose failure behavior
sections.intro: A failed cleanup, backup, update, copy, or sync attempt can change the state or block the next safe step.

blocks.title: Choose the post-failure boundary
blocks.description: The recommended choices keep a failed case inspectable and prevent a silent retry or a wider delete batch.

fields.label: 1. What should Tessera do after a failed transaction?
fields.description: The failure may have changed the path, owner state, sync state, or usable space.

options.label: Pause and inspect
options.description: Save the exact scope and error, re-measure, and ask before retrying or changing the plan.

options.label: Retry same plan
options.description: Try the same operation again when the failure looks temporary, while keeping the existing confirmation.

fields.label: 2. How should Tessera explain the blocker?
fields.description: The next safe step depends on whether the cause is measurement, permission, sync, backup, or an owner app.

options.label: Show blocker and owner
options.description: Name the failed transaction, exact blocker, measured state, responsible owner, and one safe next step.

options.label: One generic next step
options.description: Keep the result short and suggest one broad action such as rescan, restart, or try again.

fields.label: 3. Should Tessera do work in the background after failure?
fields.description: Users report losing trust when a cleanup or sync action continues without a clear visible state.

options.label: No background work
options.description: Stop mutation and monitoring after the result unless the user starts an explicit, local observer.

options.label: Allow quiet observer
options.description: Keep a local, read-only observer running to report whether space or owner state changes.

fields.label: Your notes
fields.description: Tell me what Tessera should show or save when the first cleanup, backup, update, copy, or sync step fails.
fields.placeholder: For example: stop, explain the exact blocker, save the case, and never try a wider delete without asking.

sections.title: Next loop
sections.intro: The evidence loop stays open while the agent builds.

items: Use the implementation handoff as the build contract for the read-only slice.
Submit the two open forms. The next page will keep your answers read-only.
Manually code the 5,005 GitHub candidates before using them as behavior evidence.
Continue with issue pages 11 and later when older history can change a product decision.
Add direct owner documentation and user reports for communication storage before adding an adapter.
Re-scan the real macOS path after each feature slice and record new questions.
